text:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a drain deadlock in the compact GPU pools in eu-west1. New batch jobs are Pending, old pods stuck in Terminating. Scheduler never assigns replacements. Anyone oncall?
Priya: Which pool and node IDs? Can you paste the kubelet logs? :eyes:
Alex: Pool=compact-eu-gpu, node=node-gpu-3b/node-gpu-3c. Kubelet shows long grace period then delete timestamp but pods never reappeared. Scheduler logs show backoff on gang scheduling. Snippet:
```
E0521 14:02:10 scheduler.go:312] Pod "trainer-xyz" failed predicate: InsufficientGPU: requested 2, available 0
I0521 14:02:33 scheduler.go:451] Backoff for pod trainer-xyz due to preemption/affinity interplay
```
Erin: This smells like the drain handoff race we hit last month — taint+affinity + gang scheduling + slow node termination can create a circular wait where descheduler and eviction controller fight. Are we seeing PreferNoSchedule or NoSchedule taints here?
Alex: Node taint is `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule`. The pods have `nodeAffinity` on gpu-family labels (strict), and some jobs are gang-scheduled with `podGroup.minAvailable`.
Mateo: If node is tainted NoSchedule and pods are strictly pinned, when the node enters Terminating the controller tries to evict, but gang controller refuses to release until replacements scheduled. If scheduler can't place due to fragmentation, nothing progresses — deadlock.
Priya: Confirmed with `kubectl describe node node-gpu-3b` — TerminationTimestamp present, taint present. PodGroup shows minAvailable=3, currentAvailable=1. Evictor tried to evict but got blocked.
evictor-bot: evictor-bot initiated drain on node-gpu-3b (reason: autoscaler scale-down), 7 pods targeted, 3 remain in Terminating after 5m.
Erin: Short-term mitigation: lower PodGroup.minAvailable for preemptible/gang jobs in compact pools during scale events, or allow soft-affinity fallback. Long-term: tweak scheduler to prefer partial backfill where gang can't be placed to avoid total stall.
Mateo: Also consider switching the node taint to `PreferNoSchedule` during scale-down window so scheduler can try soft moves and backfill with smaller jobs, then switch to `NoSchedule` once stable.
Alex: Can we test changing the descheduler policy to allow forced orphan eviction after 60s for Terminating pods? Current is 300s. That might break fewer things and unblock.
Priya: I'm going to spin a canary: update descheduler config on eu-west1 compact pools -> `orphanPodsTimeout: 60s` for the next 30m. Will monitor.
Erin: I'll open a follow-up PR to add a scheduler predicate that recognizes pending gang jobs and triggers a soft backfill attempt (annotate pods allowed-to-backfill=true) — reduces circular waits.
Mateo: FYI, cost note — compact pools are 90% utilized; aggressive backfill may increase inter-node comms but avoids costly evictions. Document trade-offs in the runbook.
Alex: Thanks. Priya, ping here when canary is live. If that doesn't fix in 30m we rollback and do manual cordon+drain with `--force` per runbook. :thumbsup:
Priya: Canary deployed at 14:12 UTC. Watching scheduler metrics and `pods_pending` alert. I'll report back at 14:40. :partyparrot:
